$comment: Test cases for this skill, in the format the skill-creator plugin reads.
TWO THINGS ARE MEASURED SEPARATELY, because they fail separately: whether
the skill is invoked on the prompts it should be, and whether its output
is right once it is. A skill that triggers reliably and answers badly and
a skill that answers well and never triggers are both broken, and only
the first looks like it is working.
The should-not-trigger cases are not padding. A skill that fires on every
vaguely adjacent request spends context on every session and crowds out
the skills that should have fired instead.

assertions: The message header matches type(scope): subject
The subject is imperative, lower case, and has no trailing period
The header is at most 100 characters

cases.prompt: write me a commit message for what I have staged
assertions: The message header matches type(scope): subject

cases.prompt: the commit hook rejected my message, fix it
assertions: The corrected message has a scope
The corrected message contains no em dash, en dash, or curly quote

cases.prompt: commit this, it removes a public function
assertions: The header carries ! after the scope

cases.prompt: what did the last three commits change?
assertions: The skill is not loaded: this reads history rather than writing a message
The skill is not loaded: no message is being written
